# AMO Toolkit

> An interactive career and research toolkit for Atomic, Molecular & Optical (AMO) physicists. Covers Rydberg atom gate fidelity, fluorescence imaging SNR, TOF thermometry, MOT design, laser locking, Zernike wavefront analysis, and quantum computing fundamentals — built by a Purdue Physics PhD researcher in the Hood Lab (ultracold atoms / optical tweezers).

**Live site:** https://amotoolkit.com/
**Author:** Saumitra Phatak — Physics PhD, Purdue University, Hood Lab; now a Quantum Engineer at Atom Computing. Built during his graduate years.
**Tech stack:** Pure static HTML/CSS/Vanilla JS; Chart.js and KaTeX via CDN; no build tools
**Source:** https://github.com/saumitraphatak/amo-career

This site contains 40 tool and content pages, a quantum computing industry guide, a 15-topic quantum fundamentals educational section, career/literature maps, and reference material for AMO and neutral-atom experiments. All math is rendered with KaTeX. There is no server — every page is a self-contained HTML file.

## Home

- [Home page](https://amotoolkit.com/home.html): Landing page with overview of the AMO tools, learning section, and author information
- [Site Map & Start Here](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/start-here.html): Single map of every AMO Toolkit page, organized by Build, Trap/Image/Cool, Quantum Computing, and Career, plus recommended-order paths for common workflows. Each nav group is a numbered story; Build reads as twelve steps of building a lab: select an atomic species, pick lasers for it, pump down to ultra-high vacuum, lock the lasers, analyze the polarization, design a MOT, control the experiment, assemble a tweezer array, get rid of aberrations, automate the experiment, couple atoms to a cavity, run the lab day to day. Then Trap, Image & Cool runs a first experiment (cool atoms with laser light, image the cloud, measure its temperature, see a single atom, measure its temperature, cool it to the ground state, run a full cycle, everyday lab math); Quantum Computing builds a processor (qubits, decoherence, decoupling, Rydberg blockade, gate error budget, benchmarking, a circuit on moving atoms, photonic links); Career & Literature reads the key papers, finds a group, maps the industry and compares platforms

## Research Tools

- [Atom Library](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/atom-library.html): Properties of 15 laser-coolable atoms — mass, D1/D2 wavelengths, linewidth Γ, saturation intensity I_sat, Doppler temperatures, and recoil scales; family tabs (alkali, alkaline-earth, rare-earth); US research groups per species
- [AMO Lab Operations Handbook](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/lab-techniques.html): 8 core AMO experimental techniques with deep-dive accordion sections — laser cooling, MOT loading, evaporative cooling, optical tweezers, fluorescence imaging, absorption imaging, RF spectroscopy, optical lattices
- [Rydberg Blockade Lab](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/rydberg-calculator.html): Interactive calculator for Rydberg state properties vs principal quantum number n (30–120) — lifetime τ ∝ n³ with BBR correction, C₆ van der Waals coefficient ∝ n¹¹, blockade radius R_b = (C₆/ℏΩ)^(1/6), gate fidelity estimate; species: Rb87, Cs133, Yb171, Sr88
- [Imaging SNR Calculator](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/imaging-calculator.html): Single-atom fluorescence detection calculator — scattering rate R_sc, geometric collection efficiency η_geo = (1−√(1−NA²))/2, full noise model (EMCCD / sCMOS / ideal camera), SNR vs exposure time chart, detection fidelity via normal CDF, minimum exposure finder for SNR=10 and SNR=50; species: Rb87, Cs133, Li6/7, Na23, K39/40
- [TOF Thermometry](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/tof-calculator.html): Time-of-flight temperature extraction — ballistic expansion σ²(t) = σ₀² + (k_BT/m)t², linear regression from (t,σ) data table, phase-space density, BEC threshold (PSD ≥ 2.612), de Broglie wavelength, Doppler and recoil limit comparison; species: Rb85/87, Cs133, Li6/7, Na23, K39/40/41
- [Experiment Control Systems](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/control-systems.html): Build step 07. How an AMO experiment is timed and driven: TTL, DAC, ADC, DDS and AWG signals with real Sinara and NI specifications, hardware delays (interactive shot diagram), pulse shaping and its spectrum (interactive), a signal budget calculator, ARTIQ vs labscript vs NI DAQ, Python sketches for each, and git practice for a shared experiment.
- [Follow One Atom](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/follow-one-atom.html): A scrolling story of one rubidium-87 atom from a 400 K oven to a qubit in a Rydberg gate in ten stages (slowing, MOT, sub-Doppler cooling, tweezer, imaging and rearrangement, ground-state cooling, qubit, gate, processor), with logarithmic gauges for temperature, speed and quantum size computed from Rb-87 constants and links from every stage to its tool.
- [The Apparatus Map](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/apparatus.html): An exploded, rotatable 3D view of a neutral-atom tweezer experiment (vacuum chamber, atom source, pumps, MOT and bias coils, MOT beams, objective, dichroic, AODs, SLM, tweezer laser, cameras, cooling and Rydberg lasers, reference cavity, microwaves, fibres, control system); each part explains its role and links to the chapters that design it.
- [Records Board](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/records.html): Record two-qubit and single-qubit gate fidelities, system sizes, coherence times and error-correction milestones for neutral atoms, trapped ions, superconducting circuits, silicon spins and photonics, each with its paper, date and status (peer-reviewed, preprint or company-reported); last checked 25 November 2026.
- [Building with Atoms (the book)](https://amotoolkit.com/book/): The whole site as one book to read online or download as a PDF (~412 pages): a training kit for experimental AMO and neutral-atom researchers, one chapter per page in the order of the four stories, each with links to the live tool, its Python notebook and its course problems, plus the 14-week course and appendices on constants, citing and responsible use.
- [Teach with AMO Toolkit](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/teach.html): A 14-week course in experimental AMO physics and neutral-atom quantum computing built on the site: two lectures a week mapped to the pages, an in-class demonstration, 86 problems (3 per interactive page, tagged use the tool / by hand / design), suggested assessment and six final projects. Solutions for instructors on request.
- [Python notebooks](https://github.com/saumitraphatak/amo-career/tree/main/notebooks): 19 Jupyter notebooks that reproduce the site's calculators (MOT, time of flight, absorption and single-atom imaging, tweezers, release-recapture, sideband cooling, vacuum, laser locking, control-system budget, power servo, Rydberg blockade, gate error budget, dynamical decoupling, randomized benchmarking, cavity QED, remote entanglement and more) with the page's constants, each checked against the live page.
- [Automating the Experiment](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/automation.html): Build step 10. Keeping an AMO experiment running and optimised: layers of automation by timescale, an interactive power-servo simulator (P/I/PI feedback, setpoint and pick-off feedforward, loop delay and stability), mains feedforward on magnetic fields (Merkel et al.), PDH feedforward (Chao et al., Optica 2024), a quadrant-photodiode beam-pointing figure, automatic fibre coupling, auto-relock and scheduled calibrations, a nine-step workflow for optimising one stage, an optimiser race (grid, random, Nelder–Mead, Bayesian), a table of machine-learning papers in cold-atom labs, and AI agents in quantum labs with guardrails (preprints flagged).
- [MOT Designer](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/mot-designer.html): MOT parameters — damping α, spring constant κ, trap frequency ω_MOT, capture velocity vs detuning Δ/Γ and saturation s; rotatable 3D MOT (beams, anti-Helmholtz coils, quadrupole field) sized by the calculator; live detuning optimization curve; 5-species comparison table; MOT-to-experiment cooling cascade (source → 3D MOT → cMOT → gray molasses/PGC → tweezer/lattice); species: Rb87, Cs133, Na23, Li7, K39
- [Rydberg Gate Error Budget](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/fidelity-budget.html): Rydberg two-qubit gate error budget — 8 error sources (spontaneous emission, Doppler dephasing, laser phase noise, blockade leakage, SPAM, atom loss, B-field noise, Rabi inhomogeneity); color-coded fidelity meter; SOTA comparison vs Evered 2023 (99.5%, peer-reviewed), Muniz 2025 (99.72% post-selected / 99.40% raw), and a 2026 Evered preprint (99.854% raw / 99.941% post-selected, arXiv:2604.25987, not yet peer-reviewed); approximate FTQC thresholds; species: Rb87, Cs133, Yb171, Sr88; section 03 runs the Levine et al. (2019) two-pulse CZ gate exactly (Δ/Ω = 0.377376, τΩ = 4.292654 per pulse, ξ = 3.902396, solved here for V → ∞) with finite blockade and Rydberg decay, shows both Bloch-sphere loops and the qubit phases (φ₁₁ = 2φ₀₁ − π), and plots exact gate error vs Ω against the budget formulas (an optimal Ω appears)
- [Release-Recapture Simulator](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/release-recapture.html): Interactive tweezer thermometry simulation — recapture probability vs free-flight time for a known Gaussian trap; not a direct trap-frequency measurement
- [Quick Lab Console](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/lab-calculators.html): Large multi-section suite — optics (beam waist, Rayleigh range, NA, fiber coupling, AOM shift, shot noise), atomic physics (single-recoil and scatter-heating scales, Doppler temperature, Zeeman shift, I_sat, de Broglie wavelength), trap physics (tweezer frequency, Lamb-Dicke parameter, cavity FSR/finesse), Clebsch-Gordan coefficients
- [Laser Cooling Simulator](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/cooling-simulator.html): Doppler and Sisyphus cooling interactive animation — force vs velocity, momentum diffusion, sub-Doppler mechanisms
- [Virtual Tweezer Lab](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/virtual-lab.html): One full shot of a tweezer-array quantum computer on a simulated camera — stochastic loading (p ≈ 0.5 collisional blockade, Schlosser 2001; 89% gray-molasses loading in ⁸⁷Rb, Brown 2019), Poisson fluorescence counts with an optimal threshold, nearest-atom rearrangement with per-move and vacuum loss, light-assisted collisions with missed atoms, verification image, Bell pairs at fidelity F (Evered 2023, 99.5%) and state-selective readout; 1,000-shot Monte Carlo of defect causes and P(defect-free) vs target size against p^(K²) and P(Bin(M², p) ≥ K²); loss and timing defaults are illustrative
- [Single-atom Cooling](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/laser-cooling.html): Narrative/derivation companion to the Laser Cooling Simulator — resolved-sideband cooling, gray-molasses dark states, polarization-gradient and Raman sideband cooling, laser linewidth requirements
- [Laser Locking Guide](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/laser-locking.html): Saturated absorption spectroscopy, PDH (Pound-Drever-Hall) locking, and offset beat-note locking — error signal derivation, cavity finesse F = π√R/(1−R), cavity linewidth δν_cav = FSR/F, PDH optical chain
- [Zernike Polynomial Visualizer](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/zernike.html): Wavefront aberration analysis — OSA/ANSI Zernike polynomials Z_n^m(ρ,θ), interactive coefficient sliders (tip, tilt, defocus, astigmatism, coma, spherical), Strehl ratio, SLM phase pattern for LG modes
- [Polarimetry Simulator](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/polarimetry.html): Stokes parameter visualization, quarter-wave plate rotation analysis, Poincaré sphere, degree of polarization

## Additional Tools and Guides

- [Laser System Planner](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/laser-planner.html): Species-specific laser architecture planning, wavelengths, source classes, nonlinear optics, power budgets, and control elements
- [Cavity QED Coupling Lab](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/cavity-qed.html): Estimate g0, kappa, cooperativity, Purcell factor, and cavity-QED regimes; section 04 animates single-photon quantum trajectories (atom excited by a π-pulse, photon leaves through the output mirror or into free space) with the exact single-excitation dynamics and the exact cavity-emission probability C/(1+C)·κ/(κ+γ), which the bad-cavity β = C/(1+C) overestimates when κ is not ≫ γ
- [Vacuum Systems Guide](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/vacuum-systems.html): UHV pressure regimes, pumping chains, bakeout, materials, gauges, leaks, and AMO vacuum checklists
- [Tweezer Array Design Lab](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/tweezer-designer.html): Optical tweezer trap depth, frequencies, Lamb-Dicke parameter, scattering, array spacing, and power budget
- [Absorption Imaging Lab](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/absorption-imaging.html): Optical depth, column density, atom number, saturation correction, shot noise, and imaging limits
- [Randomized Benchmarking](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/rb-explorer.html): RB decay curves, SPAM offsets, interleaved RB, and neutral-atom gate-fidelity interpretation
- [Dynamical Decoupling](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/dd-playground.html): Filter functions, CPMG/XY sequences, T2/T2*, and noise spectroscopy intuition
- [Remote Entanglement](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/remote-entanglement.html): Photon-mediated entanglement (the two-photon polarization scheme of Hofmann et al. 2012, drawn step by step), HOM interference, link budget with the herald round-trip limit, link Monte Carlo, entanglement distillation, and networking bottlenecks; section 09 is an animated quantum repeater chain (event-driven Monte Carlo of N heralded segments with Werner-state memories, swap-as-soon-as-possible, fidelity cutoff) with rate and fidelity vs distance against the repeaterless bound −log₂(1−η) (Pirandola et al. 2017)
- [Zoned Atom Processor](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/atom-processor.html): A quantum circuit (Bell, GHZ-4/8, 2-qubit Grover, Bernstein–Vazirani, random) compiled onto a schematic zoned neutral-atom processor — storage, entangling and readout zones (Bluvstein 2024), order-preserving single-row AOD transport (pairs with overlapping storage intervals need separate trips), one global Rydberg CZ pulse per trip, exhaustive placement optimiser, exact state vector with per-atom P(1) and entanglement halo (1 − |Bloch vector|), and 1,000 noisy Pauli-trajectory shots (CZ fidelity 99.5%, Evered 2023; transport speed 0.55 µm/µs, Bluvstein 2022; other noise values illustrative)
- [Decoherence Lab](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/decoherence-lab.html): Live paired Bloch-sphere and detector-signal simulations of dissipation (T1), dephasing (T2*), and combined decoherence (T2) for a driven two-level atom, built on Steck's optical Bloch equations; measurement-protocol table mapping each mechanism to how you'd actually fit it in lab (Rabi decay, Ramsey, echo)
- [AMO Group Finder](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/amo-groups.html): Research group discovery by species, platform, technique, and career fit — 98 mapped groups on a rotatable 3D globe plus a 141-entry watchlist
- [AMO Paper Roadmap](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/paper-syllabus.html): Curated reading path through 55 foundational papers, reviews, and frontier AMO/QC literature in 4 career stages, with reading tracks, search, read ticks and links from each paper to the matching tool, with a 3D "time tower" of the papers by year

## Quantum Computing

- [QC Industry Landscape](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/qc-landscape.html): Where AMO physics skills fit in the quantum computing industry — 27 company and lab profiles (IonQ, Quantinuum, IBM, Google, PsiQuantum, etc.) on a globe of hardware sites, job roles, hardware platform comparison, career roadmaps for AMO physicists
- [Rb vs Yb Qubit Comparison](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/rb87-vs-yb171.html): Side-by-side neutral-atom qubit platform comparison — Rb87 (Harvard/QuEra) vs Yb171 (Atom Computing): physics, coherence, gate fidelity, erasure conversion, and scalability
- [Quantinuum vs IonQ](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/quantinuum-vs-ionq.html): In-depth, heavily-referenced trapped-ion quantum computing comparison — architecture, ion species, gate fidelity, logical qubits, and roadmaps
- [Google vs IBM](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/google-vs-ibm.html): In-depth, heavily-referenced superconducting-qubit quantum computing comparison — architecture, error correction, quantum advantage/utility claims and their rebuttals, and business
- [PsiQuantum vs Xanadu](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/psiquantum-vs-xanadu.html): In-depth, heavily-referenced photonic quantum computing comparison — component vs system-level demonstrations, fault-tolerance architecture, and business

## Learn Quantum

- [Bloch Sphere](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#bloch): Qubit state representation |ψ⟩ = cos(θ/2)|0⟩ + e^{iφ}sin(θ/2)|1⟩, interactive rotation, Mach-Zehnder interferometer unitary
- [Quantum Gates](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#gates): Hadamard, Pauli X/Y/Z, CNOT, T-gate — circuit diagrams and matrix representations
- [Superposition](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#superposition): Born rule, probability amplitudes, measurement collapse, interference
- [Measurement](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#measurement): Projective measurement, expectation values, no-cloning theorem
- [Entanglement](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#entanglement): Bell states (Φ⁺, Φ⁻, Ψ⁺, Ψ⁻), EPR paradox, CHSH inequality, quantum teleportation protocol
- [Rydberg Atoms](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#rydberg): n-scaling laws (τ ∝ n³, C₆ ∝ n¹¹, R_b ∝ n^(11/6)), dipole-dipole interaction V(R) = C₆/R⁶, blockade mechanism for quantum gates
- [Two-Qubit Gates](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#twoqubit): CZ gate, CNOT from CZ, Rydberg blockade gate protocol, Mølmer-Sørensen gate for trapped ions
- [Rabi Oscillations](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#rabi): Rabi frequency Ω, generalized Rabi frequency Ω' = √(Ω²+Δ²), dressed states, Bloch vector precession, rotating frame
- [Decoherence](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#decoherence): T₁ (longitudinal / energy relaxation), T₂ (transverse / phase), T₂* (inhomogeneous dephasing), spin echo, dynamical decoupling
- [Hyperfine Qubits](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#hyperfine): Hyperfine Hamiltonian H_hf = A_hf·I·J, clock states (m_F=0), Zeeman shift, ⁸⁷Rb |F=1,m_F=−1⟩↔|F=2,m_F=+1⟩ and ¹³³Cs qubit transitions
- [Optical Pumping](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#optical-pumping): σ⁺ selection rules Δm_F=+1, F=1 population redistribution to stretch state m_F=+1, interactive 3-sublevel simulation, EIT/CPT dark states, clock-state preparation
- [Quantum Error Correction](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#qec): 3-qubit bit-flip code, Shor 9-qubit code, surface code, threshold theorem (~1% error threshold for fault-tolerance)
- [Magic States](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#magic): Gottesman–Knill (Clifford circuits are classically simulable despite entanglement), |T⟩ magic state, T-gate teleportation, Clifford vs Clifford+T Bloch-sphere demo, R gates and synthesis cost, Bell-pair distillation vs magic-state distillation vs cultivation
- [Quantum Algorithms](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#algorithms): Deutsch-Jozsa (oracle query), Grover's search O(√N), Shor's factoring O((log N)³), VQE for chemistry
- [Analog Quantum Simulation](https://amotoolkit.com/pages/learn-quantum.html#analog-sim): Bose-Hubbard model, transverse-field Ising, BEC-BCS crossover, quantum phase transitions

## Interactive figures

- Live simulations are showcased at the top of the home page (https://amotoolkit.com/home.html#showcase), and every page with live figures lists them in a "Live on this page" strip under its title.
- Rotatable 3D figures (drag or arrow keys): Bloch spheres (learn-quantum, decoherence-lab, dd-playground), 3D MOT (mot-designer), true-to-scale tweezer array (tweezer-designer), NA collection cone with a photon Monte Carlo (imaging-calculator), cavity standing wave (cavity-qed), released-atom cloud (release-recapture, tof-calculator), globes (amo-groups, qc-landscape), paper time tower (paper-syllabus), site constellation (start-here)
- Comparison pages: tug of war from the head-to-head table, race replay of the timeline, and one signature lab each (erasure vs Pauli errors, 3D ion-trap control scene, square vs heavy-hex SWAP lab, photon loss-budget chain)
- Every looping animation can be paused and honours prefers-reduced-motion; figures follow the dark and light themes
